title: Short-term GPU leasing & brokerage flow
content:
Summary:
This working sheet defines the operational flow, decision heuristics, and unit-economics for short-term GPU capacity acquisition via leasing and broker channels as an alternative to immediate capital orders. Purpose is to bridge 2–12 week gaps in committed fleet availability (new SKUs or delayed shipments) while minimizing cost and operational risk.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers regions: us-west, us-east, eu-west, ap-south.
- Lease target window: 2–12 weeks. Brokerage/spot-lease for <4w, managed lease contracts for 4–12w.
- Typical SKU classes considered: A100 80GB, A100 40GB, H100 80GB, L4 24GB.
- Burn-rate baseline: current production steady-state 24k token-GPU-hours/day (internal metric).
- Safety buffer policy: trigger when projected days-of-capacity falls below 18 days at current burn.

Decision heuristics (quick reference):
1) Trigger evaluation: days_of_capacity = onhand_hours / burn_rate_hours_per_day. If days_of_capacity < 30 -> run fast-eval.
2) If days_of_capacity between 18–30: prefer short-term lease for critical regions only (us-west/us-east), use brokerage if price delta <25% vs ordering accelerated freight.
3) If days_of_capacity <18: open emergency procurement lane + mix of 50% lease + 50% expedite order depending on SKU lead-time.

Brokerage vs Managed Lease tradeoffs:
- Brokerage (spot) pros: fast (1–7 days), flexible returns, cheaper capex markup for short windows. cons: variable health, network/handover overhead.
- Managed lease pros: guaranteed uptime SLA, vendor-managed logistics, consolidated billing. cons: min 2–4 week notice, higher weekly rate, attachable support costs.

Operational checklist (on broker/lease selection):
- Confirm SKU firmware/driver compatibility and required kernel patch levels.
- Verify KV cache persistence and ephemeral nature of leased nodes (we prefer ephemeral for canary workloads).
- Benchmark a representative micro-batch: p50 latency and throughput on leased instance within 24h of delivery.
- Security: ensure leased nodes placed inside Redwood-managed VPC peering or private link; no external services by default.
- Billing: require weekly invoice with per-hour reporting and tagged by route/model for cost attribution.

Price heuristics and quick math examples:
- Example: A100-80GB expedited order landed in 8w costs $11k/unit. Managed 6-week lease for same SKU priced at $2.1k/week (6 wks = $12.6k) -> order cheaper if timeline >5w.
- Brokerage: spot lanes ~ $900–1.6k/week depending on region and seasonality. Use a region multiplier: eu-west *1.15, ap-south *1.35.
- Decision rule: if lease_total_cost < (expedite_order_cost * 0.9) choose lease. If >=, choose expedite order and use short broker coverage for immediate <2w gap.

Regional constraints and routing:
- ap-south: limited H100 availability; prefer temporary A100 mixes and adjust model batch sizes.
- eu-west: customs/transport adds 6–10 days to orders; prefer leasing for 4–8 week outages.
- us-west: best brokerage liquidity; maintain a private list of 3 preferred brokers.

Risk and failure modes:
- Health variance: leased GPUs may have higher silent error rates. Mitigation: run ECC diagnostics + stress test on arrival; keep a 48h burn-in pool.
- Contract dispute: require SLAs in managed leases for replacement within 72h.
- Network segmentation drift: onboarding checklist must validate VPC/subnet assignment and route tables to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

Contacts and vendors (internal shorthand):
- BrokerA (preferred): ops contact Marcos / brokerA@vendors.example.com — fast lane, us regions.
- LeasePartnerX (managed): account lead Priya / leaseX@vendors.example.com — quoted managed SLA.
- Logistics: FreightOps team (Slack: #freight-ops) for expedited shipments.

Action items (owner, due):
- Marco: maintain broker availability matrix, update weekly (due: recurring).
- Sofia: build automated cost comparator webhook for quick-eval (due: 2024-10-15).
- Devon: integrate leased-node health checks into onboarding playbook (due: 2024-10-01).
- Aisha: ratify regional multiplier table with finance and add to this doc (due: 2024-10-08).

Appendix — quick-eval checklist for on-call:
- Step 0: run current-days-of-capacity computation.
- Step 1: open eval sheet (link in linked_artifacts), fill SKU, desired weeks, target regions.
- Step 2: run cost comparator (broker quote, lease quote, expedite-order estimate).
- Step 3: select lane, open procurement ticket with expected acceptance criteria and benchmark test.
- Step 4: send notice to SRE and platform-engineering for network onboarding.

Notes (working thoughts):
- Long-term: consider a negotiated standing lease agreement during seasonal demand peaks to lower weekly rates and reduce friction.
- Consider instrumenting a "lease health score" from bench results to build a reputation profile for brokers.

This is a working document: please add broker notes, real quotes, and post-mortem summaries here.
